title: Extension by zero and lower shriek (finite coefficients)
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category.

For an open immersion $j\colon U\to X$, the *extension by zero*
$j_!\colon\Sh(U_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)\to\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal A)$ is
sheafification composed with the left Kan extension along the opposite of the
localization functor $U_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{proét}}$,
$(T\to U)\mapsto(T\to U\to X)$. It is left adjoint to the pullback $j^*$ of
[def-sfb-finite-upper-star], exact, and fully faithful.

For a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{i}\bar X\xrightarrow{g}Y)$ of $f\colon X\to Y$
[sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], put $f_!^c:=g_*\circ i_!$. For $f$ admitting a
compactification, the *lower shriek* is $f_!:=f_!^c$ for a chosen compactification $c$
of $f$. There is a canonical natural transformation $f_!\to f_*$, and it is an
isomorphism when $f$ is proper.

proof.text: Use the construction of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero]: for the localization $\ell:(T\to U)\mapsto(T\to U\to X)$, define $j_!=\operatorname{sheafify}\circ\operatorname{Lan}_{\ell^{\mathrm{op}}}$ on the underlying presheaf of a sheaf. This is exactly the extension-by-zero functor in the statement, on the chosen small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

The statement of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction] gives $j_!\dashv j^*$ and identifies $j^*$ with restriction, $(j^*G)(T\to U)=G(T\to U\to X)$. The finite-limit preservation and exactness assertion is precisely [lem-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-exact], and full faithfulness is [lem-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-fully-faithful]. These results apply with the same Grothendieck abelian $\mathcal A$ and the given open immersion; no finiteness condition on $\mathcal A$ or on $U\to X$ is added.

source.place: First sentence: adjunction, exactness and full faithfulness

proof.text: For a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{i}\bar X\xrightarrow{g}Y)$ as in [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data], compose extension by zero along $i$ with the direct image along $g$. The construction [def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek-compactification] gives $f_!^c=g_*i_!$; [def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek] fixes $f_!=f_!^{c(f)}$ for a chosen compactification. All these are functors between the fixed-$\mathcal A$ sheaf categories, with $g_*$ as in [def-sfb-finite-lower-star].

source.place: Second sentence: the two compactification definitions

proof.text: Write $\delta:i^*i_*\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathrm{id}$ for the invertible counit furnished by [def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek-to-lower-star], and $\epsilon:i_!i^*\to\mathrm{id}$ for the counit of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. The natural comparison at $F$ is $\alpha_F=\epsilon_{i_*F}\circ i_!(\delta_F^{-1}):i_!F\to i_*F$. Applying $g_*$ and then the sectionwise associativity isomorphism $g_*i_*\cong f_*$ of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp] gives the natural transformation $\iota_f:f_!\to f_*$ of [def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek-to-lower-star]. This defines the map for the chosen compactification without claiming compactification independence.

source.place: Last sentence: construction of the comparison

proof.text: Suppose now $f$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. The factorization $X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}X\xrightarrow{f}Y$ is a compactification by [sk-def-nagata-sketch-data]. For any chosen compactification $c$, $g$ is proper, hence separated. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-to-separated] to the $Y$-morphism $i:X\to\bar X$: its composite to $Y$ is the proper morphism $f$, so $i$ is proper. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-closed-image], $i(X)$ is closed. It is also open because $i$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Thus, identifying $X$ with its open image $U\subseteq\bar X$, the complementary subset $W=\bar X\setminus U$ is open; write $j:U\hookrightarrow\bar X$ and $k:W\hookrightarrow\bar X$.

source.place: Final properness clause, expanded in prop-sfb-finite-lower-shriek-proper.proof.md, first paragraph

proof.text: For a sheaf $F$ on $U$ and $T\to W$, restriction [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction] and the direct-image formula [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] give $(k^*j_*F)(T)=F(T\times_{\bar X}U)=F(\varnothing)=0$. Here the fibre product is empty since $T$ maps into $W$, and the empty covering of the empty scheme forces a sheaf's value there to be terminal in $\mathcal A$, hence its zero object. Reversing $j,k$ gives $j^*k_*H=0$ for every sheaf $H$ on $W$. These equalities hold as sheaves, since the component identifications commute with restriction and all maps between zero objects are unique.

source.place: Final properness clause: second bullet of the clopen argument

proof.text: Using $k^*\dashv k_*$ from [def-sfb-finite-upper-lower-star-adjunction] and $j_!\dashv j^*$ from [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction], for every $H$ on $W$ we have $\operatorname{Hom}(k^*j_!F,H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_!F,k_*H)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F,j^*k_*H)=\operatorname{Hom}(F,0)$, a singleton by step 6. Thus $k^*j_!F$ is initial, so it is the zero sheaf (the objectwise zero sheaf is both initial and terminal). Consequently $k^*\alpha_F$ is a map between zero objects, and is invertible.

source.place: Final properness clause: third bullet of the clopen argument

proof.text: For completeness, the unit $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to j^*j_!$ of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction] is invertible using [lem-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-fully-faithful] as follows. Put $L=j_!$, $M=j^*$. Fullness gives $v:MLF\to F$ with $L(v)=\epsilon_{LF}$. Faithfulness and the first triangle identity give $v\eta_F=\mathrm{id}$; naturality of $\eta$ and the other triangle identity give $\eta_Fv=ML(v)\eta_{MLF}=M(\epsilon_{LF})\eta_{MLF}=\mathrm{id}$. Thus $\eta$ is an isomorphism. Applying $j^*$ to the formula of [def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek-to-lower-star], the factor $j^*\epsilon_{j_*F}$ is the inverse of $\eta_{j^*j_*F}$ by the triangle identity, and the other factor is $j^*j_!(\delta_F^{-1})$, also invertible. Hence $j^*\alpha_F$ is invertible. This checks the actual comparison map, not merely the existence of some isomorphism between its source and target.

source.place: Final properness clause: first bullet of the clopen argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism] on $\bar X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ to the two objects $U,W$. They cover the site in its stated sense: for every object $V\to\bar X$, the opens $V_U=V\times_{\bar X}U$ and $V_W=V\times_{\bar X}W$ cover $V$. The pro-étale covering definition [def-weil-pbc-proetale-covering] is satisfied: the maps are open immersions, hence weakly étale, and every affine open of $V$ has a finite subcover by affine opens contained in $V_U$ or $V_W$ (take the affine-open basis refinement and use quasi-compactness of that affine). Their sieve is contained in the sieve of objects admitting a map to $U$ or $W$, so the latter is covering. To identify localized restriction with $j^*,k^*$, an object over $U$ in this localized site is a factorization $T\to U\to\bar X$; its map to $U$ is the base change of $T\to\bar X$ because an open immersion is a monomorphism: after identifying $U$ with the open subscheme given by [def-weil-open-immersion], a morphism into $U$ over $\bar X$ is uniquely determined by its composite into $\bar X$. The fibre-product universal property therefore identifies $T\times_{\bar X}U$ with $T$. It is therefore weakly étale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change]. Conversely composition takes a pro-étale object over $U$ to one over $\bar X$ by the localization construction of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero]; morphisms and covering families are unchanged. Thus these localized restrictions are exactly the sectionwise restrictions of [def-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-adjunction], and likewise for $W$. Steps 7 and 8 now imply $\alpha_F$ is invertible for every $F$. Its inverses are natural (the naturality square for $\alpha$ can be multiplied by the component inverses), so $\alpha:j_!\to j_*$ is a natural isomorphism.

source.place: Final properness clause: joint conservativity on the two-open cover

proof.text: For the open immersion $i$ of the chosen compactification, step 9 gives the invertibility of $i_!\to i_*$. Applying the functor $g_*$ preserves its inverse, so $g_*i_!\to g_*i_*$ is invertible. Composing with the isomorphism $g_*i_*\cong f_*$ of [def-sfb-finite-lower-star-comp] proves that the precise comparison $\iota_f$ defined by [def-sfb-finite-lower-shriek-to-lower-star] is an isomorphism whenever $f$ is proper.

source.place: Final properness clause: apply g_* and the composition isomorphism
